validity.researcher_notes: Existence and identity confirmed independently of GEM: a Russian federal government territorial-planning decree (sudact.ru, item 31 of the trunk-gas-pipeline schedule under Government Order 816-r) names this exact project and route; independent regional press (newsvo.ru 2016, vologda.mk.ru + vologdaregion.ru 2020, TASS via Wayback 2016) and a primary operator source (mrg.gazprom.ru, Gazprom's Vologda gas-distribution subsidiary, via Wayback) all corroborate the same project under the same name/route across a 2016-2022 span. Status=operating for Stage I specifically is independently confirmed by the mrg.gazprom.ru source, which states gas reached Kirillovsky District (this stage's terminus) by end of 2021. TWO CAVEATS surfaced during this sweep and recorded separately: (1) a Diameter unit discrepancy (530mm vs the sheet's 500mm) resolved as a units-convention non-issue -- 530mm is the standard OUTER diameter for Ду500/DN500 nominal pipe under GOST 31447-2012/20295-85, not a different pipe; (2) a genuine SegmentCost concern -- the only source giving the exact 22,000,000,000 RUB figure on the sheet states it explicitly as the FOUR-STAGE PROJECT TOTAL, not a Stage-I-specific cost (see the separate 'concern' validity record, contested=SegmentCost). Also note: this project's own primary/operator sources (mrg.gazprom.ru, vologdaregion.ru) describe capacity and route figures at the whole-project (all 4 stages / 412 km) level far more often than at the per-stage level GEM records; the Capacity fill on this row applies the whole-project 743 million m3/y figure to Stage I under a reasoned uniform-diameter/constant-capacity exception, flagged there and here for a human reviewer's judgment rather than silently applied.

So the two figures describe the same pipe under different diameter conventions, not a material spec conflict.
